It should be possible to use gitlab's "git blame" to find the original

hi @moshekaplan - would you please help me to find a person in gerrit who can provide a draft with more details? thanks in advance. And also, do you really think I need to explain to user what counts, average and other columns mean in that stats window? That's excessive imho.

Alas, the furthest I got with git blame is where Gerald Combs migrated the code from GTK.:
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/commit/ea28298e961bca09a4294a4130463ea54123fa14

However, if you look at the history of packet-ancp.c, the file containing the protocol dissector and statistics code: https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/commits/master/epan/dissectors/packet-ancp.c

you can see that ANCP was added in 2010 with this bug: https://bugs.wireshark.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=4590 . In Bugzilla, "Aniruddha" wrote the following:

Protocol:
--------
The Access Node Control Protocol (ANCP) is a standards based protocol intended to facilitate the transmission of control and dynamic subscriber configuration information between an access node (DSLAM) and a L3 subscriber aware controller (BRAS/NAS).
It is a TCP/IP based protocol using GSMPv3(RFC 3292) messages.
Uses TCP port 6068.

Dissector:
----------
The dissector can dissect the following ANCP messages now:
 - Adjacency messages
 - Event Messages (Port Up/Down)
 - Port Management messages
And adds statistics for the same.
thank you @moshekaplan - this info is also in the Wireshark wiki. I will add the information about messages

I think that this description, while not helpful to someone who knows nothing about protocol, is an improvement over the previous state. @moshekaplan do you have an example trace file or protocol insight that could help?

+The Access Node Control Protocol (ANCP) is an TCP based protocol, which operates between an Access Node and Network Access Server. The Wireshark ANCP dissector supports the listed below messages:
